facts.fact: ANEC's director-general Matar Ndao told a press conference on 5 November 2025 that the NEKKAL application is deployed in 400 civil-status centres, from which the central civil-status database is accessible; he gave no total number of centres.

ANEC's director-general said on 5 November 2025 that the central civil-status database is accessible from the NEKKAL application in the 400 centres where it is deployed, and spoke of a 'network of civil-status centres connected to NEKKAL'; the article does not say in terms that acts are entered in it at registration.

On 5 November 2025 the director-general of ANEC, an agency attached to the ministry of Urbanisme, Collectivités territoriales et Aménagement des territoires, stated that NEKKAL is the only civil-status management tool recognised by the government.

On 5 November 2025 ANEC's director-general called on mayors still using 'clandestine' civil-status management software to stop and to join the network of centres connected to NEKKAL, and reported 20 million acts digitised, indexed and loaded into the national civil-status register and a user platform designed for remote requests.
